panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra reads the nineteen-day replacement ETA at the active maintenance bracket. Zib continues his practical examination without looking at her.
PANEL 2 — Two-shot at the unit: Zib explains the temporary repair needs to be safe and documented. Astra refuses to treat delayed procurement as permission for unapproved improvisation.
PANEL 3 — Jax arrives with a handheld reader, already pulled into the real repair. Astra points to the unit, and Jax makes the joke about washing the reader himself.

PANEL 4 — Pixa opens the proper temporary-material authorization beside Astra and Zib at the workbench. Its overbuilt paperwork contrasts with the modest physical repair; the discussion stays among the three visible coworkers.
PANEL 1 — Mira watches the revised brace finish a second ordinary test cycle while Zib checks the measured load, no spectacle.
PANEL 2 — Zib holds up the conventional brace and points to the stable support; Mira confirms the narrower result at the same workbench.
PANEL 3 — Astra listens from the edge of the service bay as Mira relaxes slightly at the measured result. Astra cautions against claiming a new industry from one held test.
PANEL 4 — Brick records THE WEIRD THING GOT A JOB in his notebook while Mira gives him a dry look; the punch line belongs to their exchange, not a crowd.
PANEL 1 — Glorp at the maintenance terminal points to the empty applications field. Kreeb listens beside him; the operating bay remains visible beyond them.
PANEL 2 — Close on the report's single demonstrated application while Kreeb points to the one line actually supported by testing.
PANEL 3 — Mira faces Glorp and Kreeb, allowing herself to be pleased about the limited material result without claiming to understand its wider applications.
PANEL 4 — Astra joins the small group, steering the report away from describing the crew as a manufacturing input. Keep the service unit behind her in the same bay.
PANEL 5 — Glorp glances at Astra over the draft wording; the correction is a dry procedural exchange, not a new committee meeting.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks toward the stabilized temporary brace after the banter. Her dry response belongs in an isolated closing portrait with the working unit behind her.

summary: An ordinary working report narrows a promising temporary repair to one demonstrated application. Glorp, Kreeb, Mira and Astra contribute in turn rather than crowding the same terminal, and Mira ends by looking back at the functioning unit.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the maintenance terminal, Astra expands the notice of commercial feasibility interest; Mira stands beside her to read it.
PANEL 2 — Tight view of the commercial-interest language beside a note recording only one demonstrated temporary use. Astra takes in the disproportionate framing.
PANEL 3 — Mira insists on joining the feasibility call because the work is hers. Astra answers that she should, and acknowledges Mira's ownership rather than postponing the decision.

PANEL 4 — Astra looks through the glass at the still-functioning maintenance bay; Mira warns that the people on the call may misunderstand the small result. Astra's final dry promise lands with both faces readable.
